events_chronological: On a southern beach a woman notices a man who is holidaying at the same hotel with his girlfriend.
The girlfriend flies home after a row, and the man knocks at the woman's door that evening.
The two of them wade out into the sea together as the sun goes down.
At their wedding in a country hotel her estranged parents are seated at opposite ends of the table and every speech is cold.
He passes out drunk on the wedding night, and she lets a stranger in from the corridor.
Their son is delivered by emergency surgery while the father sits in the car park unable to make himself go inside.
He arrives on the ward hours later and admits where he has been.
Over dinner for his brother and his brother's boyfriend, he describes watching strangers have sex at a club.
She says at the same table that she was there and watched too, and the evening turns.
The couple begin sleeping in separate rooms, and he takes a lover at his office.
A clerk in a lawyer's office reads out the terms of the divorce and the two of them sign it.
They take a hotel room afterwards, sleep together one last time, and he dresses and leaves her lying on the bed.
nonlinear_category_reason: Scene order runs from the latest stretch to the earliest throughout, with no present-day level the telling returns to. Five episodes reverse a marriage: the divorce, a dinner, the birth, the wedding, and the day the two met.
syuzhet_notes: Five self-contained episodes play in reverse, each opening after the one before it has already been undone: the divorce first, the first meeting last. Nothing in the telling ever moves forward between episodes.
fabula_notes: Each episode is a single continuous stretch, so its own bullets play in order; the reversal operates entirely at the level of the five episodes.
